 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet Six South African players feature in Season 5 squads © Cricbuzz Six South African players feature in Season 5 squads © Cricbuzz For the last four seasons, South African players have had to stay out of the ILT20 because of the overlapping window – the SA20 invariably clashed with the UAE league. This time, the congestion has been avoided, allowing some of South Africa's top players to feature in the tournament, which begins in Dubai on Saturday (November 21). Heinrich Klaasen and David Miller are excited about the opportunity.
 “Yeah, obviously. I have heard a lot about it (the league)," said David Miller, one of the leading finishers in T20 cricket. “I have been to Dubai quite a few times and played a lot of cricket here in the past. Not so much in the last couple of years, but before that, I played quite a lot of cricket here.”
 Miller also feels the presence of South Africans makes the competition stronger. “I would definitely say so. Having a lot more overseas players to choose from definitely makes the tournament stronger. South Africa has done really well over the last period of time and has added a lot of quality to world cricket. So, it definitely strengthens the tournament.
 “The tournament itself, with so many overseas players in each team, creates really good competition. I have wanted to be a part of it for a long time. With the schedule for the year, which includes all the different leagues, international cricket and so on, it does become quite difficult to schedule these sorts of tournaments. I am here this time because it does not overlap with the SA20. I am really happy about it.”
 The ILT20 runs from November 21 to December 20, while the SA20 is scheduled to take place from December 26 to January 25.
 Klaasen, a former World No 1 T20I batter, is excited to be competing in the league, which he says is among the ‘top four or five’ in the world. “I know it's a good, strong competition. You just can't walk in here thinking you're going to score runs and perform. You really need to be at your best. That's also one of the biggest reasons why I wanted to come and play in this league. It's among the top four or five leagues in the world.
 “ For me, it's more a case of not playing international cricket or franchise cricket back home. This is an international window in South Africa's schedule, so that opened up a big window for me. That's why I'm available for this league.
 Klaasen is the captain of the captain of the Adani Sportline owned Gulf Giants, the champions of Season 1. But having retired from international cricket, he knows it will not be easy for him. “You can't just turn up and expect to perform. There are quality players in all the leagues. There are ways to simulate the intensity at which you need to train. If you just go about things without really caring and simply turn up for tournaments, you're not going to be successful. 
 “You have to do your work, maintain your fitness, train hard enough and get your skill levels right. I'm experienced enough to know what I need to do, what I need to train for and where I need to put in the work. I've also got enough contacts and analysts to know what preparation I need. So, if I keep doing my work and my homework, I should be fine."
 Six South African players feature in Season 5 squads. Apart from Klaasen and Miller, Faf du Plessis (Dubai Capitals) Tabraiz Shamsi, (Gulf Giants), Lizaad Williams (MI Emirates) and George Linde (Sharjah Warriorz) are the other four.
